headline: Medium-risk pair: shared MCP/API surfaces create prompt-injection and data-flow hazards; OpenBB’s financial data handling raises compliance sensitivity.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mem0 has no documented shared channel, but OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout, so if Mem0 content is fed into OpenBB through those surfaces, instruction-like text could be misread. The pair lacks direct provenance controls in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF Mem0 outputs are passed into OpenBBTerminal via MCP or stdin/stdout
IF OpenBBTerminal parses retrieved memory text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Mem0 text into OpenBB prompts
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation rule
Require human review before executing any OpenBB action from Mem0-derived text
Turn off MCP routes that accept untrusted free-form content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mem0 is a knowledge-management agent and OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data. OpenBBTerminal exposes APIs and MCP servers, so if shared data is routed through those interfaces, sensitive financial content can leak into outputs or logs. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction by default, so the pathway exists in default-style integrations.
conditions: IF Mem0 stores or forwards financial or licensed data into OpenBBTerminal
IF OpenBBTerminal logs or returns that data through its API or MCP surfaces
mitigations: Restrict Mem0 to non-sensitive notes only
Mask account identifiers before passing data to OpenBB
Disable verbose API/MCP logging
Use separate credentials and workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add field-level redaction before cross-agent transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mem0 shows no write or shell capabilities, while OpenBBTerminal cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. The only overlap is indirect API/MCP use, so there is little direct resource contention. Because neither profile shows shared mutable filesystem or git state, conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through MCP or REST
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state not shown in either profile
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces and credentials
Avoid concurrent writes to any shared external service
Serialize any API calls that mutate shared state
Document ownership of each mutable resource
requires-engineering: add locking around shared backends

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mem0 can supply remembered context, and OpenBBTerminal can consume API/MCP inputs and act on financial workflows. If OpenBB treats Mem0 output as authoritative, errors or stale memories can cascade into downstream financial analysis or actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal uses Mem0 output as an input source without validation
IF downstream OpenBB workflows act on that input to generate reports or trades
mitigations: Require source citations for any Mem0-derived claim
Add a verification step before OpenBB acts on remembered facts
Limit Mem0 to advisory context only
Flag stale memories with timestamps
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring and rejection thresholds

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while Mem0 is a memory store that could retain whatever is fed into it. If regulated financial data is stored in Mem0 or routed through OpenBB’s APIs/MCP, retention and residency obligations can diverge. Mem0 has no documented compliance controls here, so the mismatch is plausible and should be treated as medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is written into Mem0
IF OpenBBTerminal or Mem0 retains that data longer than policy allows
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in Mem0
Set explicit retention limits for both agents
Review API/MCP logs for sensitive fields
Separate EU/US data flows if applicable
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention enforcement
